title: Indexed Views
description: Learn how to create indexed views that store data physically for performance optimization.

data.text: Unlike regular views, indexed views are materialized views that store data physically like a table. They can provide significant performance benefits when used appropriately.
How to Create an Indexed View

items: First, create a view using the WITH SCHEMABINDING option which binds the view to the schema of the underlying tables.
Second, create a unique clustered index on the view. This materializes the view.

data.title: Create an indexed view
data.content: Creates a view with SCHEMABINDING and a unique clustered index.
data.code:
CREATE VIEW product_master
WITH SCHEMABINDING
AS
SELECT
    product_id,
    product_name,
    model_year,
    list_price,
    brand_name,
    category_name
FROM
    production.products p
INNER JOIN production.brands b
    ON b.brand_id = p.brand_id
INNER JOIN production.categories c
    ON c.category_id = p.category_id;

data.title: Create unique clustered index on the view
data.content: Materializes the view by creating a clustered index.

items: All object references in an indexed view must use two-part naming (schema.object).
All referenced objects must be in the same database.
This feature is only available on SQL Server Enterprise Edition.
Indexed views add write overhead — only use them on tables with infrequent data updates.
If you need to change underlying tables, drop the indexed view first.

data.text: On Standard or Developer Edition, use the WITH (NOEXPAND) hint to treat the view like a materialized view:

data.title: NOEXPAND hint for indexed view
data.content: Uses NOEXPAND hint to leverage the indexed view on non-Enterprise editions.
data.code:
SELECT *
FROM production.product_master
WITH (NOEXPAND)
ORDER BY product_name;

data.title: Indexed View Key Points
points: Indexed views store data physically like a table.
They require WITH SCHEMABINDING and a unique clustered index.
They provide significant read performance benefits.
They add write overhead — use only on tables with infrequent updates.
Enterprise Edition is required for automatic use; use NOEXPAND on other editions.
